pages.text: "Wow, the water left all sorts of things!" Mina searched riverbank soil. Low water exposed wide wet earth, scattered with wood and dry leaves.
Mina picked up a round green fruit. "I'm hungry. I'll eat this!" It came close to their mouth.
"No!" Experienced eldest child Raju ran over and caught Mina's hand. "Put it down! You don't know what it is." Mina stopped. "Oh? Isn't it food?"
They hurried to Mom and showed it. Taking it, she shook her head. "We don't eat this. Good that you asked."
"How can I tell what's food?" Mina asked. "Ask me first about things you don't know." Mom placed the fruit far from their hands.
Mina clasped both hands behind their back. "I'll Ask Before Eating!" Raju nodded beside them.
Later, Mina saw a soft white lump. Before, they might have grabbed it, but this time the hand stopped. "Mom, what's this?"
Mom looked. "A mushroom. Let's leave it." Mina stepped back without touching.
Raju asked, "There's something over there, too?" Mina stopped their hand and called Mom. "Please look with us."
Mom lifted Mina into a hug. "Thank you for asking first." From her arms, Mina looked around the riverbank.
